bio_en: Armenak Levonian, known as Yerkat and Ashot-Yerkat, was born in 1870 in the village of Tsghak near Bitlis and emigrated young to America to support his family, joining the ARF there. In 1902 he left America and went via Geneva to Van; after three months in the plain, at the end of 1903 he led a 12-man band to Akhlat to spread the idea of arming among the people and link Van and Sasun. Trapped in a cave with explosives, his band blew up the surplus charges and broke through the Kurdish cordon, killing about 55 Kurds including noted chiefs, but seven Armenians fell, among them Yerkat; his grave is unknown. Droshak mourned him in March 1905.
notes: Compiled from the archive review, 2026-10-12. Confidence: medium. Death year inferred (late 1903-1904).
